headline: Peru's Amazon trial shows basic income transforms food security
meta_description: A two-year basic income trial in Peru's Amazon gave 211 Indigenous people £2 daily, cutting food insecurity from 73% to 26%.
summary_short: 211 Indigenous people in Peru's Amazon received £2 a day for two years. Households unable to afford nutritious food dropped from 73% to 26%.
body:
A world-first basic income trial in Peru's Amazon has delivered striking results: households unable to afford nutritious food fell from 73% to 26% among 211 Indigenous participants over two years of receiving about £2 daily.

The trial demonstrates the concrete impact of unconditional cash transfers on the most vulnerable communities. Beyond hunger reduction, 87% of participants took part in rain—a detail suggesting the program enabled people to engage more fully in community and cultural activities rather than being consumed by survival needs alone.

These outcomes challenge assumptions about how aid works best. By trusting Indigenous communities with direct cash rather than conditional programs or in-kind assistance, the trial shows dignity and autonomy can coexist with measurable improvement in nutrition and wellbeing.
quick_facts: 211 Indigenous people in Peru's Amazon received the trial
£2 per day for two years was the payment amount
Food insecurity fell from 73% to 26% among households
87% of participants took part in rain
